text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Export of liquefied petroleum gas from Chevron's Escravos field may soon begin. About 8,000 barrels per day will be exported.
- Ethnic bickering may stall a proposal to build a pipeline to gather natural gas associated with oil production from a Royal Dutch/Shell field near Nembe.
- Fuel shortage worsens in administrative capital Abuja.
- More than 200 workers of Oluwa Glass have been laid off. A company spokesman said a reduction in business over the past few months was responsible for the need to cut the workforce.
- Bomb experts in southeastern city of Port Harcourt probe Wednesday's explosion.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) saved $36 million by insuring its assets with a consortium of companies rather than with state-run National Insurance Company of Nigeria.
- Chairman of Bureau of Public Enterprises, Hamza Zayyad, has advised the government against divesting from oil production joint-ventures. THISDAY
- Government gives United States more information on a spate of terrorist bomb attacks in Nigeria. Police say they want to pursue their investigations in the United States.
